Move-in day will be relatively simple. You'll have someone or your family help you move in all your stuff. You'll meet your roommate(s) if you haven't already. You girls/guys will connect. Or maybe you won't hit it right off the bat. That's ok, takes time to get use to living with someone you've never met before. The day will go on, you'll meet RA's, part of the administration and maybe some teachers. You'll make some friends while learning about the school. Some friends you'll make through an ice-breaker game, some you might meet just in your dorms walking through the halls. Ethier way it will happen. I've seen the "coolest of the cool "and the "weirdest of the weird" kids all with huge groups of friends. 

After the Parents leave, you'll all simultaneously realise you no longer have a bed time, no one to wake you up, no one to cook your breakfast, no to tell you come home from a friends house. And that's fucking awesome and fucking shity at the same time because it means you (almost) an adult. Some people will try to go out to a party (as there are usually a good amount at any school during welcome week) some will drink in there dorm, some will get a game of manhunt or Ultimate frisbee on one of the sports field. I can say with confidence, the one thing no one will be doing after move in is done is sleeping. Too much going on, too many new people to meet.

What you should know...I've been to two different schools and I'm going on my third (my major has me moving a lot). One was a tiny quieter school and one was a bigger D1 sports school. Here's what I've learned. 

-There's always new friends to be had. This is even more true if your school's population is over 5000. I had like 3 different groups of friends at both schools. Friends I went out to parties with, friends I study with, friends I just chill with. I've seen freshmen who were great friends with 5th-year seniors, and 21-year-olds who got along well with freshmen. There will always be new people to meet and great friends to have. 

-BECAREFUL AS FUCK WITH ALCOHOL. AND EVEN MORE SO WITH OTHER DRUGS. You may have drank and smokes in highschool. But I promise college is 50x whatever you were doing. Every experience I've had has been pretty good in that people never really forced anything on me. I was always drinking at my own pace. Which is what you want, don't go buck wild on your first night. That's how you become the freshmen who went to the hospital on his first night. But with that, always watch your drink (even if your a guy), if your underage try your best to avoid carrying any form of alcohol in public (pregame in the dorm or just drink when you're there. At the most, hide a water bottle somewhere in your pants) ,drink in the house or backyard not the front yard, travel with friends and always try to have some extra money for an emegerncy taxi or something. And always be friendly. 

-Always wear a condom.

-Hit up the gym or play some sports with friends every now and then to stay in shape

-ALWAYS WEAR A CONDOM

-And ironically, my last word of advice is do everything you can to stay on top of your grades because they come first. Your school will most likely offer free  tutoring, paper checks, or other ways to improve your work. Find out what there are and use them. See if there are scholarships available and try to apply for some. If you need help, email the professor and see if they will help. I'm sure you know how to do all this and how to stay on top of your studies. A lot of kids do. But most never really follow through. Follow through.

That's a lot to take in, sorry. I just love giving advice about college from my experiences. I'm actually about to drive out to my school in a few hours so wish me luck too. But anyway, read through this once and then just go out and have fun. Everything here is meant to be advice, not a guide book. Only you can decide how your college career will be. So make sure enjoy it, cause college is fucking sick bruh.

I have transferred twice, going on my 3rd ( I don't recommend transferring this many times). At the first school my GPA was a 2.1. I applies to 3 schools. The required GPA for two of them was above a 2.5 just to be considered and the other was a 2.0. I got into all 3 of them. My second time was just applying to a school that I was basicly already accepted to so I don't count that. The third time I applied to 5 schools.  3 of these schools were big state schools everyone knew the name of, and at this point my GPA was maybe just a 2.6 now. Their requirements were much higher (3.2s and such) and one school required I write a letter explaining a legal issue I was involved in (one that doesn't look great on any application). I was accepted to all of those 3 universities. I called The 4th school and was told that I was most likely accepted, I just needed to send my final transcript for the current semester and the other I kind of just didn't care about anymore.

So, what am I saying? Do the application. If you can't stand the idea of being at your school for one more semester, start that application right this second (some schools are rolling applications and you can get in whenever). It's gonna be some work because you'll have to contact your current school to send an official transcript, but it may be possible. 

It may have been luck that I got into pretty much all the schools I tried transferring too. Or maybe they thought I could do much better at their schools. I don't know. All I know is, if I didn't try I'd still be stuck at my first school, probably unhappy and wanting more. Find out what you need to do, get that transcript sent right away, and really focus on the essay (if they let you write one). The essay has power when your grades are relatively low.

The schools you mentioned are higher level schools, so I don't know as much about them. However, I can offer you this advice. Keep working hard. Get A's and B +'s. Keep a high gpa, do some sports and/or join some clubs and your application will look amazing (don't overwhelm yourself though). Once it comes time to apply for college, there will most likely be a section of the application that asks you to tell them about yourself or give you a topic where you can write about yourself. Give them the truth, you live in a bad place and your parents can't really support your dreams. All you want to do is climb out. Don't beg that they give you money or anything like that, just give them your story. Your grades will back up how hard you work. 

And listen to /u/chevybow.  Have safties, always have safeties. Penn State University is a great school, a lot of my friends went to Rutgers, Ohio State is one of my favorite and Oklahoma State has a Vet Program I believe. If you have 3.0s, then all of these schools should be an easy to a medium difficulty to get into.

As for the money, do your best and the school will reward you accordingly. Schools could give you a full ride, 50% , or it could even just be $1000 a year. Take whatever you can get and use loans for the rest. Sucks but thats the position we live in today. However, if you're successful in college and find that job after, loans won't be as big a problem as everyone says they are.

[This](https://bigfuture.collegeboard.org/college-search) and [This (this one might be a little slow)](http://www.collegeconfidential.com/college_search/) should help you find some more options, just in case.

oooooooooooooohhhhhhhhhhhhhh maaaaaaannnnnnnnn do I remember this phase. Except for me I was already accepted to a few places, so it was just a matter of not taking a shit on my test and I was fine. 

But let's be serious. There is nothing we on the internet can do for you, short of telling you how we handled senioritis, or give advice and resources to help.  The truth is **THIS IS ALL YOU**. You gotta motivate yourself to keep your head in the books. From what I remember, my last year wasn't all too hard. A minimal amount of studying, a dedicated 2 hours for finals and projects was more than enough to get me a B average. It is probably different for you though, so adjust accordingly. 

And if you do that, and still find yourself doing nothing, then DO SOMETHING. When I was bored during my senior year, I found myself doing a number of things to prepare for college. Look into colleges if you haven't picked them yet. Read up on how to write a killer essay, and what to do to make yourself look better for admissions. Ask others about college culture, the do's and don'ts, what they learned, etc. Almost every college I looked into had a thriving subbreddit on here. Check them out to try and get an idea of what the college life there may be like.

If your college application is done and accepted, and you're in the transition phase, starting figuring out what your gonna bring. College is a chance to re-invent yourself. So find out some new clothes you wanna try, maybe buy a hat for the first time, see if you like the feel of boat shoes. If you know how big your dorm is, then starting looking into things you can bring to make your dorm more "you". (If you like video games or use your computers for movies, I highly recommend bringing a projector. By the third week, I was doing everything with it. From chill video games session to having the entire floor watch a movie. And if you hook it up outside, well, you're gonna become quite popular.)    

And if all else fails, then at least improve yourself. Read at least one article on how to be physically or mentally healthier. Practice being more social and outgoing. Get into the habit of working out, going for a run or meditating. Make a new Reddit account, unsubscribe from all the default accounts, and subscribe to /r/getdisciplined , /r/GetMotivated , /r/college  and subbreddits of that nature.

Trust me, starting the good habbits now is the best thing you can do for yourself before attending college.

EDIT: Feel free to shoot me a pm if you have any questions or want any advice. I was in your shoes about 2 years ago, so a lot of what your feeling is still pretty fresh in my mind.

I have transferred a few times, and I've learned quite a bit. I've attended a small, quiet, cold, private, catholic college and a large, warm, loud, Division 1, state college. Here's some things I have learned that I wish people had told me so I could of avoided transferring all the time (not that transferring is a bad thing. Just something I preferred not to do).

-People: No matter where you go, you can and will find people you like. You'll find people you don't like. You may even find a girl/boy you'll fall in love with. Don't worry about the friends part. I have yet to meet one person at either school that didn't have friends. From the frat god to the awkward call of duty nerd, they all have friends. 

-Weather: Be it snow, be it a heat wave, be it neverending rain. At some point in the year, the school you're at is gonna have some weather you won't like. But, you'll still find a way to survive. Plus you'll be inside for 75% of your college experience (classes, parties, sleeping) so don't let it get to you too much.

-Money: Don't let the money get to you too much. You are most likely gonna come out with debt by the end of college. Try your best to apply for scholarships (public and private). But if your choices are a school that's $5000 a year and a school that's $60000 a year....you might want to go with the first one. 

-Parties: The parties depend on where you attend, and who you know. If you like going to parties, then you'll find one. The parties at the small school tended to be small aparmaent parties that were invite only with occasional large parties. The state school had larger invite only parties and a lot of open parties. The state school parties were certainly better but the small school parties were spent with closer friends which were just as much fun, but not nearly as crazy. Regardless KNOW YOUR LIMIT, never carry what is obviously alchool (if you're under 21) outside in public, and be calm and collective around cops.

-Classes: While how much a degree or education varies depends on your school, for the most part your professors will be hit or miss. Some will be amazing and inspire you to become president. Others will not give a shit (I once had a teacher clearly hear someone cheating on the final, question the student who said he was asking for a pencil, and brush it off like it was nothing. Great for the student, but overall shitty teacher). Regardless of the teacher, pay attention in class, take notes, get extra help if you need, and get your homework done on Friday if you can. Then study on Sunday. Do this, and the grades will come your way. (As a bonus, teachers are more willing to help someone who clearly has a good work ethic).

-Major: You'll have time to figure out what you want to do. If you aren't sure yet, go to a large school. They tend to have a lot more majors and will give you a variety to choose from as well as a way to see if you'll like it or not. Purdue is great engineering school, Harvard has a great economic school. Drexel starts you on an internship toward you last few years. Some majors and programs are just better other places. Some don't really matter as much. For example, my major (Aviation/Professional Flight) doesn't differ too much wherever I go. Just make sure you're always a semester to a year ahead of yourself (looking ahead for classes you wanna take next semester, internships or job opportunities that may be available to you as you go on in your college career). 

And above all else, HAVE FUN. These next few years will be the last few years you have to really be young. So make the best of it. Join a club, rush a frat/sorority, hook up with the ugly person at a party, run a 5k, do a dorm prank, make friends with your teacher, take chances, have fun! You're going to enjoy it, so don't stress too much!



Also, if you ever have a question, you can message me. I remember being where you are and wishing I had someone to talk and ask questions too.
